Venezuela

How many left

Venezuelan emigration according to each source

Top, stock: people born in Venezuela living in the destination (Gaskin and Abel on 1 January; UN DESA at mid-year; R4V only people registered by each government; censuses on census day). Bottom, flow: people who moved from Venezuela to the destination during the year.

Reading. Gaskin and Abel estimate 8.1 million people born in Venezuela living abroad on 1 January 2024; UN DESA, 8.3 million in mid-2024. R4V counts only registered people in 17 countries.

Sources. Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Annual flow by country of previous residence (mig_prev). Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Stock by country of birth (stock_mean), as of 1 January. United Nations, DESA, Population Division (2024). International Migrant Stock 2024. Population born in Venezuela by country of residence. R4V Platform. Refugees and Migrants from Venezuela, population registered by the governments of 17 Latin American and Caribbean countries, Feb 2018 – Aug 2026. Accessed 11 Oct 2026. INDEC (Argentina). Censo Nacional de Población, Hogares y Viviendas 2010 and 2022. Population born in Venezuela, own processing. INE (Chile). Censo de Población y Vivienda 2024. Population born in Venezuela, own processing.

Arrivals, departures and return

Departures: people moving from Venezuela to another country. Arrivals: people moving to Venezuela, split into those born in Venezuela (return, flow by country of birth) and those born elsewhere. Net: arrivals minus departures.

Reading. Since 2013, the net balance has been negative every year. In 2018, 2.6 million left and 11,353 Venezuelans returned; in 2021 returns reached 148,646.

Sources. Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Annual flow by country of previous residence (mig_prev). Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Flow by country of birth (mig_brth); return = people born in Venezuela arriving in Venezuela.

Where to

Where Venezuelans emigrate to

Annual flow of people moving from Venezuela, by destination country. The seven main destinations of 2015–2023 are shown; the rest are in Others.

Reading. In 2018, 2.6 million people emigrated from Venezuela; 28% went to Colombia.

Source. Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Annual flow by country of previous residence (mig_prev).

Where they live today: the 12 main countries

People born in Venezuela by country of residence (UN DESA, mid-2024) and Venezuelans registered by each government (R4V, latest data).

Reading. In Peru, UN DESA estimates 1,596,667 people born in Venezuela in mid-2024 and R4V records 1,630,258 in 08/2026. The United States and Spain are not covered by R4V.

Sources. United Nations, DESA, Population Division (2024). International Migrant Stock 2024. Population born in Venezuela by country of residence. R4V Platform. Refugees and Migrants from Venezuela, population registered by the governments of 17 Latin American and Caribbean countries, Feb 2018 – Aug 2026. Accessed 11 Oct 2026.

The Venezuelan star: destinations by period

Cumulative flow of people who moved from Venezuela to each destination in the period. Each country's arc is proportional to what it received. Labels inside the figure are in Spanish.

Reading. Colombia received 15.5% of Venezuelan emigration in 1995–2002 and 38.4% in 2015–2023.

Source. Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Annual flow by country of previous residence (mig_prev).

Venezuela within the regional system

Cumulative flows in the period between South American countries and their main destinations outside the region; in red, those of Venezuela. Corridors above 5,000 people. Labels inside the figure are in Spanish.

Reading. Flows with origin or destination in Venezuela were 3.6% of the regional system in 1995–2002 and 30.2% in 2015–2023.

Source. Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Annual flow by country of previous residence (mig_prev).

The corridor with Colombia

Venezuela–Colombia corridor

Top, people moving in each direction. Bottom, people born in Venezuela living in Colombia according to three sources.

Reading. On 1 January 2023, Gaskin and Abel estimate 1.99 million people born in Venezuela living in Colombia; R4V had 2.48 million registered at the end of 2022. The 2022 Colombia → Venezuela flow (254,685) is mostly people born in Colombia.

Sources. Gaskin, T. & Abel, G. J. (2026). Deep learning four decades of human migration. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10611-7. Annual flow by country of previous residence (mig_prev). Mobility

Mobility: trips from and to Venezuela

International visitor trips with origin or destination in Venezuela, summed over the countries with data. It is a lower bound.

Reading. Trips from Venezuela reached 3.9 million in 2018 and fell to 0.6 million in 2020. Arrivals in Venezuela have no data after 2017.

Source. Grohmann, T., Recchi, E. & Bernasconi, L. (2025). The 10 Billion Travel World: Continuity and Change in Global Transnational Mobility (1995–2022). Global Transnational Mobility Dataset (GTMD2). International visitors (gtmd2_vflow_int); corridors without data are not added.

The grey band in the charts marks 2022–2023, years in which the data may be distorted by the Gaskin and Abel model adjustment.

In the Venezuelan case, the 2018 and 2019 flows cannot be separated precisely. The model estimates the stock at 1 January of each year and the flow is the difference between two consecutive years, so in reality the jump may be spread across both. The size and direction of the change do not depend on that assignment.
